pr_body:
It turns out that the old geo_line has a bug whereby it can cause the truncation to happen in the middle of the line instead of from one end. This occurs if there are documents with missing sort field and other documents with missing points, and the data is distributed across multiple shards. Each shard gets a leaf-reader and collects into a bucket with the size truncated to the documents with sort-field (ie. not requiring existence of point field). This means the per-shard geo_line can be shorter than the size limit. That extra space can be filled during MergeGeoLines from a shard that could be far away, so not the correct globally sorted document set.

Fixing this properly requires changing the BucketedSort.Leaf to truncate on both sort field and point field, but that code is currently used by all aggregators, so we either have to confirm that it is OK for other aggregators to get this change in behaviour, or override that leaf.collect() method for geo_line only.

Fixes #96909

comments: The error description `GeoLine[sort=asc, use-timestamps=false] is complete: expected false but is true` means this test is checking the old algorithm (time time-series is not used when use-timestamps is false), and passing in more data than the size limit, so should be truncated, but is not. I'll test locally and see what is going on. I know not all documents have data, but the fraction that has data is deterministic, so should not cause this.

review_comments: This is the workaround. Since the bug causes truncation to happen in the middle of the line instead of the end, we just need to test the correct end of the line. Since the documents with missing points are always 1/3 of the documents (see TestData class), we can be sure the first 2/3 of the line is good. So we test the first half only. We need to do this for both the points and the timestamps, since they are correlated and the issue will come through on both.
This mistake was hiding many failures! So two bugs in the tests, one hiding (mostly) the other.
